nodes.name: Willow
nodes.desc: Willows are shrubs and trees of damp ground and are recorded near the park. Local people collect shrubs for fuel and winter fodder.

nodes.name: Mountain grasses
nodes.desc: Red fescue and other grasses form the pasture that wild mountain herbivores and livestock graze.

nodes.name: Wormwoods
nodes.desc: Aromatic shrubby Artemisia species grow on the dry slopes. A tarragon relative is a recorded food plant of the Old World swallowtail.

nodes.name: Ephedra
nodes.desc: A low, leafless shrub of dry rocky ground whose berries are eaten by Himalayan snowcocks.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: Lives on steep slopes and scree. It eats alpine grasses and herbs, and in winter more twigs and needles of trees such as willow.

nodes.name: Urial
nodes.desc: A wild sheep native to the Hindu Kush and nearby ranges, found on grassland, open woodland and gentle slopes.

nodes.name: Silver mountain vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of rocky mountain ground, recorded near the park. It eats plant material and is prey for foxes and snakes.

nodes.name: Gray dwarf hamster
nodes.desc: A small seed- and plant-eating rodent recorded near the park. GloBI records red foxes eating it.

nodes.name: Himalayan snowcock
nodes.desc: Listed as an Important Bird Area species at Band-e Amir. Eats grass shoots, seeds, Ephedra berries and Artemisia leaves, and golden eagles sometimes take adults.

nodes.name: Old World swallowtail
nodes.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars eat plants such as Artemisia. GloBI records many songbirds eating it.

nodes.name: Lesser whitethroat
nodes.desc: A very commonly recorded warbler near the park. It hunts insects in shrubs and is eaten by red foxes in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Black redstart
nodes.desc: An insect-eating songbird of rocky ground, recorded often near the park.

nodes.name: Long-tailed shrike
nodes.desc: A predatory songbird that hunts large insects and small vertebrates from perches.

nodes.name: Himalayan agama
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard recorded near the park that feeds mostly on insects.

nodes.name: Central Asian sand boa
nodes.desc: A small boa that ambushes small rodents and lizards, recorded in the area.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: GloBI records it eating many songbirds and small rodents recorded here. It also scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: The northern regions of Afghanistan are described as strongholds for wolves. Wolves chiefly hunt hoofed mammals and eat carrion, and the ibex has wolves as a main predator.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Occurs in Hindu Kush mountain habitat and hunts rodents, gamebirds and sometimes larger prey. It sometimes preys on adult Himalayan snowcocks.

nodes.name: Winter snow and ice
nodes.desc: Winters are severe, with temperatures down to about minus 20 C, and the lakes freeze over. Meltwater feeds streams and pasture.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: High-altitude sunshine drives plant growth in the short summer.

nodes.name: Travertine lake water
nodes.desc: Mineral-rich water deposited calcium carbonate that built the travertine dams holding the six lakes, which sustain the shoreline vegetation.

nodes.name: Mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin mountain soils hold nutrients for shrubs and grasses and are replenished by decomposition.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
